title: A Boy Walked Nine Hours to Audrey Hepburn's Door by Mistake
title_alternatives: A Boy Walked Nine Hours to Audrey Hepburn's Door by Mistake
He Was Told Not to Come Back With It. So He Walked 30km.
The Address Did Not Exist. He Was Fifteen and He Kept Going.
Nine Hours, Thirty Kilometres, One Parcel, and the Wrong Day
He Could Have Gone Home at Half Past Ten. He Didn't.
description:
At twenty past seven on the morning of the third of October 1962, a boy of fifteen was given a brown paper parcel, an address on a torn piece of card, and three instructions. Deliver it by hand. Deliver it to the person named and to nobody else. Do not use the tram.

The third instruction was the one that mattered, and nobody explained it to him. The tram fare was forty lire, and forty lire was needed for something else that week.

The address did not exist. Not hard to find — it did not exist, because that street stopped at number sixteen and had done since before the war. The housekeeper had copied the number of the house the letter came from instead of the one it was going to.

He established that at ten past nine. A sensible boy goes home at that point. Nothing would have happened to him; nobody would have thought less of him, because nobody would have thought about it at all.

Instead he spent from half past ten until twenty past five working the problem rather than the street — a parish priest who was out, a bar, a tobacconist who knew the name well enough to say it back with the stress on the right syllable, a clerk who checked a register he was not supposed to check, and four districts with no way to narrow them except by walking to each one.

He got the door right on the second try. Then it opened, and it was the wrong person, and it was the wrong day.

What he did next is the whole story, and so is what the woman who opened the door did about it.

This story is a work of fiction. Renzo, the parcel, the errand and every detail in it are invented, created for storytelling and not drawn from any record.
